summary: Perceived inference slowdowns and timeouts traced to client SDK retry/backoff and connection pool exhaustion
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sudden increase in end-to-end inference latency and intermittent request timeouts from our hosted API. Server-side traces show normal token generation times but the client is seeing large delays (hundreds to thousands of ms) before requests reach the API or while streaming.

Impact:
- Multiple production customers experienced elevated 95th/99th percentile request latencies and sporadic 504 timeouts for streaming generate endpoints.
- StreamlineAI (enterprise) observed degraded UX in their chat feature during business hours; estimated ~12% request failures and +400ms median latency increase for a 10-minute window.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod-us-east-1)
- StreamlineAI using official Redwood Python SDK v2.3.1 and node SDK v1.9.0 for different services
- SDK configured in customer app to open up to 50 concurrent inference calls, with default connection pool left unchanged

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1. Run production traffic replay for their chat workload against prod endpoint (50 concurrent connections per worker).
2. Observe client-side queuing logs, retries logged and occasional timeouts.
3. Compare server-side request logs/latency headers which show normal inference latencies.

Observations / Logs provided by customer:
- Client logs show repeated lines: "Retrying request after backoff: 850ms (attempt 3)" and "Connection pool exhausted, queuing request".
- Upstream response headers include X-Server-Latency: 45ms and X-Request-ID for successful requests.
- Firewall/Network logs show no connection resets or RTT spikes.

Initial hypothesis:
- The perceived latency is client-side queuing and backoff rather than server inference slowness. Likely causes: small or depleted connection pool, keepalive disabled or short, and a retry policy that serializes retries with long backoff windows causing head-of-line blocking.

Investigation notes (internal):
- Reproduced in staging by replaying similar concurrency using the customer's SDK config. Observed the same pattern: socket creation spikes, many TLS handshakes, and repeated exponential backoff retries.
- Server metrics for the same window show normal CPU/GPU utilization and token generation times; no serving-runtime queuing observed.
- Packet captures show frequent new TCP/TLS handshakes consistent with disabled keepalive or short connection lifetime in SDK.
- Recent client SDK release v2.3.1 included a change lowering default pooled connections per host from 25 to 6 (intended to reduce file descriptor usage) and a retry policy that switched to a jittered exponential with a high cap (max backoff 2s) and retry-on-all-errors default.

Root cause:
- Combination of client SDK default change (reduced connection pool) + aggressive retry/backoff settings caused request serialization on the client side. When the pool hit the low limit under bursty load, requests queued client-side and retried with large backoff windows, producing apparent end-to-end latency and timeouts despite healthy server performance.

Workaround applied for customer:
- Instructed StreamlineAI to explicitly set SDK pool size to 50 (connection_pool_max=50) and enable keepalive in both Python and Node SDKs.
- Advised to pin to SDK v2.3.0 temporarily (prior to the default pool change) while we prepare a patch.
- Recommended changing retry policy to: max_attempts=3, retry_on=[429, 502, 503, 504], exponential_backoff_base_ms=100, max_backoff_ms=500 and disable retries for streaming requests.

Fix and rollout notes:
- Engineering confirmed the SDK defaults were overly conservative and risked client-side queuing for bursty workloads. Patch merged: github.com/redwood-inference/clients/pull/3245. Changes included restoring a sane default pool size (16 per-host), respecting keepalive by default, and tightening retry policy (do not retry streaming POSTs and cap backoff to 600ms).
- Patch released in SDK v2.3.2 (Python) and v1.9.1 (Node).
- Backend telemetry dashboards updated to include a new client-side queuing metric (sdk.connection_queue_time) and an alert to detect rising queue times in prod.

Resolution:
- Customer applied the recommended config and/or upgraded to patched SDK. End-to-end latencies returned to baseline and timeouts stopped. SRE/Support confirmed no server-side regressions.
- Ticket classified as resolved with follow-up action items below.

Follow-up actions:
- Notify all customers via release notes and changelog about the SDK default change and recommended configuration for high-concurrency workloads.
- Postmortem/confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SUPPORT/SDK+Retry+Backoff+Runbook
- Add automated smoke tests that run client concurrency patterns against a staging endpoint to detect similar regressions before releases.
- Consider telemetry changes to emit client-expected headers when SDKs detect connection pool exhaustion.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Support): Opened ticket after StreamlineAI reported increased 95th latency and timeouts. Attached initial client logs and server request IDs.

2026-03-10 - Rafael Ortiz (SRE): Reproduced locally in staging using traffic replay. Confirmed server-side latencies are normal; suspect client socket churn and retry backoff. Filed PR to tighten SDK defaults.

2026-03-11 - StreamlineAI - Sofia Martinez (Customer Eng): Applied suggested config (connection_pool_max=50) and observed immediate reduction in queuing and no more 504s. Will test upgrade to SDK v2.3.2 next.
2026-03-12 - Rafael Ortiz (SRE): Deployed SDK v2.3.2 to internal canary environments and verified fix. Closing after customer confirmation.
2026-03-12 - Maya Chen (Support): Marked ticket resolved. Customer confirmed stable for 72h post-change.
resolution: Patched SDK defaults to increase per-host pool, respect keepalive, and tighten retry policy; customer upgraded to patched SDK or increased pool size per guidance.
notes: Related to prior case SUP-8419 but root cause different: this was a deliberate default change in the SDK that had unintended effects under bursty concurrency. Internal INT-402 tracks longer-term SDK telemetry improvements.
